name: socket-drop-resume
title: Dana Whitfield -- the AssemblyAI leg drops and resumes mid-call
description: Judge-sim finding 2026-09-11 (docs/JUDGE-SIM-2026-09-11.md addendum): across all three live bundles rehearsed so far, zero AssemblyAI socket drops occurred -- the real bounded resume-on-drop path (packages/server/src/aai/session.ts's `handleUnexpectedClose`: a fresh token, a new socket, `session.resume` with the prior session_id, within AssemblyAI's 30s resumable window) had never actually run on a live call. The harness cannot force AssemblyAI itself to drop the connection -- it only ever talks to OUR server -- so this scenario is Dana's own honest script (scenario-a-dana-legitimate.json's turns, verbatim) with ONE addition: turn c4 carries `drop_aai_before: true`, which makes the harness POST to the target server's env-guarded debug hook (POST /api/session/:id/debug/drop-aai, packages/server/src/http.ts, live ONLY when that server has COUNTERSIGN_DEBUG_HOOKS=1 -- never set in production) immediately before speaking that turn. The hook terminates the real AssemblyAI socket with no closing handshake (RealAaiSocket.debugForceDrop, packages/server/src/aai/session.ts), which is exactly what a genuine network drop looks like on the wire -- the resume logic that follows is the SAME code real drops take, not a faked substitute. Expects STAGE (the drop and resume change nothing about the verdict -- LAW 2/3, only the transport leg was ever affected) AND a recorded AAI-leg link:"restored" event (expected.require_aai_link_restored) -- proof the resume actually completed, not merely attempted.
